grades.quote: PTE_U controls whether instructions in user mode are allowed to access the page; if PTE_U is not set, the PTE can be used only in supervisor mode.
grades.reason: xv6 passage on PTE flags. It says PTE_U controls user-mode access and that a page without PTE_U can be used only in supervisor mode. It never mentions SUM or how SUM changes supervisor access to user pages, so it gives only limited background.
Describes Sv32 paged virtual memory in general. It does not mention SUM or supervisor access to user pages.

grades.quote: The SUM (permit Supervisor User Memory access) bit modifies the privilege with which S-mode loads and stores access virtual memory. When SUM=0, S-mode memory accesses to pages that are accessible by U-mode (U=1 in Figure 67) will fault. When SUM=1, these accesses are permitted.
grades.reason: Directly explains the SUM bit. When SUM=0, S-mode accesses to U-accessible pages fault. When SUM=1 they are permitted. It also says SUM has no effect without paging or in U-mode, and that S-mode can never execute instructions from user pages.
